why: The inserted narrow check after C5 blocked cuts when the next token looked like the start of a clause/argument/scope, so the top-K selector moved cuts to nearby positions; that produced small improvements on some longer chunks but a net small harm concentrated in the short (≤5-word) bin where the alternatives often split enumerations or broke coordinated predicates.  The measurement is essentially neutral overall (mean ≈0) because almost as many pairs improved as worsened.
lesson: A later revision should preserve the intent of forbidding cuts before clause/argument starters but avoid forcing substitute cuts that split enumerations or separate predicates in short pieces (the short-bin harm must be controlled).
